title: A Hundred Wyrd Locations

entries.text: Abbey to the Godflesh: a rotting abbey; living flesh of a god pulses on the altar and warps reality nearby
Abstersion Pool: a crystal pool made from a god's tear; cleanses ailments; two elder dryads judge who may bathe
Ale Spring: a cold spring of lager
Altioc's Grave: sickly oaks over piled ancient warriors, weapons standing like saplings
Bathing Pools: hot-spring pools on a poplar hill; the waters have an odd property
Bauik Hive: forested mountains, foul smell, deep cracks; sweet voices call from the tunnels
Bliss Fields: thick sweet green mist, tall grass, dead barkless trees; hard to see
Boreal Woods: vast pine, spruce and larch wood; resin smell, needle-crunch
Bramble Maze: a thorn maze that shifts when unwatched and feeds on flesh
Bristlepine Grove: ancient stunted pines on a scree slope, older than memory
Broken Shrine: shattered druid altar; something ended it all in one night
Cairn of the First Hunters: stone pile, each stone scratched with a prehistoric beast
Cenotaph to a Dead Seraph: a monument carved with a hundred lines of script; a divine beast fell here
Cliffface Amphitheater: terraced bowl under a concave cliff with perfect acoustics
Clonal Forest: one tree, one root, one will, for miles; it expects respect
Collector's Statue Garden: rag-wrapped Collector wanders among alabaster statues of mortals in terror
Council of Blind Archmages: five ruined, blind, lonely archmages who will talk at length
Darkly Lake: salt-and-pepper beach, emerald-dark water
Deciduous Growth: ordinary thick hardwood forest, busy with small animals
Desolate Crater: blasted bowl where a meteor fell; ash remains buried at the centre
Devil's Garden: only larch and crabgrass grow; demonic sprites poisoned the rest
Dwelling of the Scroll Man: hermit Gallinade carves words from his skin each day; they regrow
Elk Haven: a safe creek-side grove for an elk herd
Enormous Owl Statue: a huge ivy-grown owl statue with an alien gaze
Exile's Camp: a lawless camp of renegades and criminals; tradeable if you are careful
Fairy Grove: concentric tree rings around a mushroom ring; tiny fey at their business
Fester Pond: stinking green pond with flies; things lurk in the sludge
Fields of Silence: grass dotted with dead pines; no sound can be made; a hunter's ideal ambush
The Fisher King's River: a black trench river; corpses tangle in hungry roots
Foetid Garden: pulp ground, rot, slimes and molds that cling and breed sickness
Fossil Graveyard: a collapsed slope of fossils, small and enormous
Fruit Trees of Rotten Truth: maggoty fruit; eating it gives a few useless facts, and more
Fungal Carpet: dark, spongy fungus floor; corroded gear of the digested
Giant Spider Web: silver webs and bones; the spiders will bargain for passage
Glowlight Swamp: foggy marsh, drifting bodies, lights that are lures
Gorm's Flesh Weald: the ground, trees and roots turn to flesh and vein
The Great Honey Comb: cat-sized bees and an enormous hive in a hillside fissure
The Grove of Tea and Candles: candle-lit trees and a campfire of reverent tea-lovers
Grove of the Millennia Trees: tower-sized trees, eternal dark, whole communities in the branches
Hearthstone of Frost: freezing ruined hall; one runed stone cursed by a slighted god
Hungry Ground: tiny human mouths in the soil clicking and biting
Hysterical Hermit: a mad, shouting hermit with something to trade
Idol of Bones: a tree-like heap of bones that speaks plans into your sleep
Infectious Scrawl-Stone: touching it covers you in cursed tattoos
Ire Briar: low briar that lashes when you show anger, and feeds on it
Jeweled Trees: silver-leaved trees with gem nodules in the trunks
Junkyard: a gorge heaped with ruined common goods and scavengers
Kaleidescopic Trail: a straight trail that refracts into splits and reflections the deeper you go
Knowledgeable Knotgrass: sleeping in it brings dreams of history and philosophy
Kudzu-ville: a village strangled and sculpted by kudzu
Lair of the Mega-Raccoon: a blood-rimmed cave of a legendary beast; you were warned
Log Hollow: fallen giant logs hollowed into tunnels held by skulking predators
Lost Fortress: an empty keep with its furnishings intact, as if left overnight
Mead Tree: a hollow oak full of fine mead; tapping it carries a small risk of collapse
Megacolony Mound: a bark-stripped mound of loam and insects; the queen has a plan
Megalith Circle: concentric granite slabs aligned to the stars, worn petroglyphs
Mirror Copse: trees repeat exactly; something moves off the path; perhaps a duplicate of you
Mocking Ossuary: skulls in wall-holes insult you, and know things
Moebius Creek: a freezing creek that loops back to its start
Moot of the Treefolk: treefolk elders on a hilltop deciding the Wilds' direction; they may ask for a task
Mossbed: thick moss over everything; disturbed spores choke the air
Mushroom Forest: house-sized mushrooms, glowing at night
Muulifan's Myconid Farm: a mirthful grub tends rows of every mushroom, magic or mundane
Old Growth: a primordial, root-like, hungry growth draining colour and air
Owl Gryphon Lair: a mountaintop nest of carcasses; a giant owl-gryphon sleeps by day, with eggs
Palace of Antlers: a gorge palace of stacked antlers; its mad hunter stalks the halls
Pete's Shack: a legendary moonshiner's hill shack, rival of Petunia
Petrified Forest: stone trees marked by something that lived when they did
Petroglyph Cove: a river cave you reach by swimming under a cliff into a carved antechamber
Petunia's Shack: a legendary moonshiner's hill shack, rival of Pete
Pit of Bodies: a pond-sized pit of rendered bodies, grey mud
Plummeting Waterfall: a high waterfall and rocky pool
Ponderous Silhouette: a cliff that looks like a thinking face from one spot
Prehistoric Butte: a sheer volcanic plateau with no handholds; rumour says something is on top
Quail God: a dog-sized, gold-lit divine quail with its flock; it brings life where it walks
Quarry: a deep marble quarry with a flooded floor, nesting birds, trapped creatures
Respite of the Grey Knight: a silent tarnished knight meditating on a mountain of blades
Returning Mound: a cherry-crowned mound in a flowering glade; an unflowered tree and something at its base
Scrawl Trees: pines carved and painted with thousands of stories by crimson-cloaked carvers
Shale Field: treeless splintered shale; a fall cuts to the bone
Singer's Domain: a copse without animals; travellers dream of a high hollow song
The Slate: roots converge on a huge crude slate megalith
Sleeping Linnorm: a vast wyrm asleep like a mossy log; waking it risks its fury
Smoldering Woods: ash-black woods crawling with cinder trails; cursed by some power
Soot Crag: sooty crag over a burning coal seam venting gas
Spike Throne: a thorn-and-bramble throne in a fly-ridden fen
Spiral Earthwork: a giant salt-and-stone spiral for some ceremony
Switchback River: a slow river that doglegs into rocky rapids
Talisman Garden: thousands of hideous charms hung in the canopy, chiming
Tar Pits: bubbling asphalt that drags down the heavy; old and new remains
Time-warped Weald: plants age and regress in minutes; staying is dangerous
Tomb of the First Mortals: a crawlspace tomb of skeletons in primitive jewelry
Torpid Marshlands: a stagnant fen; leeches make boats the only way
Trees Marked by a Dark Touch: a trail of dead earth and tarry handprints; something terrible passed
Vast Mound: a man-made hill, hollow inside, a ritual space
Vermin Fields: ground of cracking bones and hiding vermin; best not stay after dark
Watching Trees: lone trees whose bark grooves fold open as glassy eyes
The Weaver's Den: a woven den of twine and web, previous heroes bricked into its walls, spider-things on patrol
Wyrd Stones: carved shale pillars; a caster studying them a week learns their secrets
Yaruinne's Haven: a dragon impaled on a tree, healed around it; she holds court and sells knowledge of great beasts

title: Wyrd hazards and traps

entries.text: Amoeba Bog: still clean water that is one giant amoeba; it lashes at anyone near and digests flesh. Detect: the water shimmers like jelly. Avoid: throw bait to distract it. Crows: A RR each exchange in reach; tier 1 1d6 acid, tier 2 half

Blistering Ivy: star-leaved ivy; touch gives painful blisters for days. Detect: nature knowledge or experience. Avoid: no skin contact; herbal soap cures. Crows: S RR; tier 1 a bane on tests for 1d3 DT-days, tier 2 one test

Bonemeal Quicksand: scree of animated bones; harmless if you keep moving, drags you down if you stop. Detect: anything dropped sinks. Avoid: cross without stopping. Crows: A RR; tier 1 pinned then dragged under, 2d6 crushing a turn until two tier 3 RRs; tier 2 pinned

Cutting Scrawl: carved runes that hurt and wipe the last hour from your mind if read. Detect: magic, or reading it. Avoid: close your eyes. Crows: M RR; tier 1 1d6 psychic and lose the last hour, tier 2 lose the hour

Doom Stones: a standing stone with a bound fiend that presses on minds nearby. Detect: soft horrid voices. Avoid: holy symbol; holy water for an hour. Crows: M RR; tier 1 one random madness, tier 2 a level of cruelty (Miasma, R27) for the day

Drowning Pond: animals sing a charming chord so you walk in and drown. Detect: music too perfect; skeletons in the weeds. Avoid: sing worse, or better. Crows: M RR after a minute; tier 1 compelled to the pond bottom, tier 2 one stumble in

Euphoria Stream: warm teal stream whose drug absorbs through skin. Detect: drug-den air; drowning flies. Avoid: no skin contact. Crows: S RR after a minute; tier 1 happy and useless for an hour, tier 2 a bane for the hour

Fen of Thievery: a gold-flecked fen that picks pockets. Detect: items on the floor; grasping water. Avoid: pay a coin first; keep valuables dry. Crows: A RR; tier 1 lose 1d3 loose items, tier 2 lose one

Flensing Grass: silver chest-high blades that slice anyone crossing. Detect: it twitches; sliced animals at its base. Avoid: fire frightens it. Crows: A RR each turn inside; tier 1 2d6 piercing, tier 2 1d6

Gallowlurks: noose-vines of a limpet creature that hoist you by the neck. Detect: intestine-like coils. Avoid: trigger from a distance. Crows: A RR; tier 1 hoisted and 1d6 strangle a turn until free, tier 2 caught but not lifted

Gluttonous Tree: carnivorous root bed that pins and crushes. Detect: slow roots, bloody bones. Avoid: climb above, or throw 100 lb of meat. Crows: S RR; tier 1 pinned and 1d6 a turn until you break free, tier 2 pinned one turn

Hallucinogenic Moss: purple moss that spores hallucinations. Detect: nature knowledge. Avoid: crude mask, hold breath. Crows: S RR; tier 1 an hour of hallucination (roll the table), tier 2 half an hour

Hideous Totems: rusted-blade totems that curse a trail so you loop back. Detect: malicious magic. Avoid: leave a weapon impaled in it. Crows: no RR; the party loops for half an hour unless it leaves a weapon
Hungry Lilies: blood-red lilies that bleed prey dry. Detect: tiny clicking teeth. Avoid: garlic. Crows: A RR each turn inside; tier 1 bleeding 1d4 a round until staunched, tier 2 one cut

Papa Sleep: a corpse dragging a grandfather clock, singing a lullaby of sleep. Detect: drowsiness and a song. Avoid: offer to repair the clock; fixing it earns a magic ring. Crows: M RR; tier 1 falls asleep, tier 2 awake but a bane until rest

Reaper's Fingers: bone-coloured toxic fungi; touch sickens, repeat touches kill. Detect: nature knowledge. Avoid: no skin contact. Crows: S RR per touch; tier 1 nauseated an hour (bane), second touch unconscious, third touch Stamina 0

Skull Children: masked spirit-children who haunt travellers with pranks nightly. Detect: laughing and skull masks in the dark. Avoid: give a toy or sweet. Crows: no RR; each night roll the prank table

Spite Beds: a bone bed that radiates hatred into the mind. Detect: nausea, dying vermin sounds. Avoid: holy water or sanctified salt. Crows: M RR; tier 1 dizzy (attacks vs you gain an edge) for an hour, a second RR to avoid rage; tier 2 dizzy only

Stink Stalks: child-high fungal stalks whose spores attract predators. Detect: bait smell. Avoid: sneak (they sense vibration). Crows: A RR; tier 1 double the encounter checks for 1d12 hours, tier 2 one extra check
Volatile Cadaver: bloated corpses that burst on touch with shrapnel and disease. Detect: pulsing seams. Avoid: throw a stone from afar. Crows: A RR; tier 1 2d6 and a disease roll, tier 2 1d6

Wyrd Flare: reality warps; entering gives a random effect from the Wyrd magic chart. Detect: magic-sense; Wyrd-attuned know. Avoid: carry a Wild Elf piece. Crows: no RR; the Ref rules a strange effect (no table in this build)

title: Wild flora

entries.text: Banshee Morel: skull-headed mushroom that wails and deafens when threatened; dried, a trumpet
Beedlesprouts: amber buds; eating them lets you hear the trees sing, shrill near predators
Boletus Posterum: pink lattice mushroom; poisonous, gives visions of the near future
Canticle Holly: blue-leaf tree with glowing berries; sleeping near it eases fatigue; berries make Saints' Respite
Carol Trees: silver-leaved conifers whose song heals but can lull you into endless sleep
Coal-nettle: foul black shrub that burns hard; ground fine it is explosive powder
Dame's Seal: elegant crimson-veined flower prized by nobles and alchemists
Deer Weed: antler-like leafless sprout that can pass as antler to the unskilled
Dirkberry: thorn bush hiding berries for fighters' brandy and a mind-freeing wine
Elf-ear: grass blade that whistles; attracts some wildlife when used as a whistle
Gristle Pear: warty tree with fat-and-gristle fruit; one feeds an adult for a day
Kingsleep Moss: soft turquoise moss; a night's rest on it is deeply restorative
Knitting Onion: onion that revives the unconscious like smelling salts
Night Cherry: black cherries causing an hour-long coma; extract is Red Slumber poison
Obsequy Ragwort: funeral flower; a body buried with it will not rise as undead
Pissboils: foul fungus that bursts into caustic liquid; causes memory loss, attracts predators, used to etch metal
Plump Friars: sweet berries; brewed into an illegal euphoria elixir
Ring Root: boiled it feeds; raw it helps neutralise poison
Scribe's Birch: bark peels as vellum-like sheets
Swineweed: stalk that burns into thick smoke causing blindness for hours

title: Wilderness diseases

entries.text: The Bleeding: you bleed from every orifice; bleeding damage is worse; can be transfused. Cure: two successes in a row, or a transfusion
Etch Mites: burrowing mites carve half-words and drawings into your skin; constant itching. Cure: three successes, or a full shave and lye bath
Fleshspawn: flesh grows out of control; each day you gain bulk until you burst. Cure: three successes in a row, or brown recluse venom; excess flesh can be cooked and eaten
Mind Drift: your soul leaves your body for an hour at a time, leaving it helpless. Cure: two successes in a day, or a day asleep under a Carol Tree
Mire Creeps: spore-filled skin balls that burst in heat for damage and spread. Cure: three successes in a row, or Pissboil salve
Treewylding: you slowly become a tree; saves only delay it; no cure but divine or great Wyrd intervention
Saint Agrella's Wart: swelling warts spread across the body, slowing and stiffening you. Cure: three successes, or a scalding herbal bath, leeching and wart removal
Scribe's Bane: you lose the ability to read and write. Cure: two successes in a row, or an eaten, ground spellbook paste
Spell-Scum: casters' spells come out random. Cure: two successes in a row, or an Oracle Sludge elixir
Vein Nettle: needle pain flares every few hours and makes every test harder. Cure: two successes in a day, or distilled Gristle Pear juice and weak acid
Whittle Worms: parasites eat nerves; you lose pain and then sight, taste, hearing, smell. Cure: two successes in a row, or a week-long surgery
The Wretches: your organs rot and you vomit them up, losing vitality. Cure: three successes in a row, or holy birch tea

note: Paraphrased from Into the Wyrd and Wild (private use, all rights reserved by the publisher). Crows conversions marked 'Crows:' are HOUSE proposals, not printed Crows rules. Crows prints no disease rule. House procedure: at each rest end the crow makes a Strength RR; tier 3 counts as a success toward the cure; tier 1 worsens the disease one step.
